note: Calibration of the money circuit for 2025 ($B nominal unless a field says otherwise; shares 0..1). Fields marked ESTIMATED in the *Notes objects are derived from 2024 values; everything else is published data or an explicit derivation documented next to it.

incomeNotes.basis: BEA NIPA 2025, pre-annual-update vintage (Q4-2025 third estimate, Apr 2026; personal income through mid-2026) so that the components share one vintage, except compensation and the after-tax profits behind corporateTaxes, which come from FRED annual series that may be a later vintage (see compensation). The Sept-2026 annual update raised 2025 GDP to $30,861.3B (gdpAnnualUpdate) and put corporate profits at $4,025.0B (corporateProfitsAnnualUpdate); component detail of that update was not available.
incomeNotes.identity: GDI = compensation + productionTaxes + netInterest + businessTransfers + proprietors + rental + corporateProfitsDomestic + govEnterpriseSurplus + depreciation; GDP = GDI + statisticalDiscrepancy (exact by construction). corporateProfits = corporateTaxes + dividends + retained (exact).
incomeNotes.compensation: Compensation of employees 2025 = $15,745.0B (51.18% of GDP), from the industries research (incomeSharesLongRun 2025 row), which takes it from FRED A033RC1A027NBEA. That series is compensation RECEIVED (national-income basis), possibly a later vintage than NIPA Table 2.6 ($15,726.9B, used in personal). It stands in for GDI compensation paid, which the research does not have for 2025; in 2024 paid exceeded received by only $22B. wages = compensation - supplements (supplements from NIPA Table 2.6).
incomeNotes.corporateProfits: NATIONAL basis (profits of US corporations incl. $526.6B net earnings from the rest of the world), with IVA and CCAdj, NIPA Table 6.16D, 2025 average of SAAR quarters. The GDI identity uses corporateProfitsDomestic ($3,550.9B, domestic industries). corporateTaxes = taxes on corporate income (FRED CPATAX-based, $695.2B).
incomeNotes.dividends: Net corporate dividend payments, all US corporations (FRED B056RC1A027NBEA, 2025, pre-update vintage). Roughly 18% of them go to foreign holders (see foreignEquityShare).
incomeNotes.retained: Undistributed corporate profits = corporateProfits - corporateTaxes - dividends (national basis, with IVA and CCAdj).
incomeNotes.buybacks: Net equity buybacks of NONFINANCIAL corporations (buybacks minus new issuance, Fed Z.1 via the US-chartbook mirror eq_payout.csv): 2025 average 1.13% of GDP. Not a NIPA income flow: buybacks are paid out of undistributed profits and borrowing, so a circuit that pays dividends + buybacks to owners should take buybacks out of retained (retained - buybacks still reinvested). Gross S&P 500 buybacks were ~$1,032B (buybacksSP500: Q1-Q3 2025 actual + Q4 estimate, S&P Dow Jones Indices); financial-sector net buybacks are not in the research data.
incomeNotes.productionTaxes: Taxes on production and imports less subsidies, ESTIMATED: BEA 2024 ($1,954.7B taxes - $94.2B subsidies) carried to 2025 at nominal GDP growth (x1.050) except customs duties, which jumped from $83.6B (2024) to ~$264.0B (2025 estimate, industries research modelPartition).
incomeNotes.netInterest: ESTIMATED: BEA 2024 net interest & miscellaneous payments of domestic industries ($611.1B) at 2024 share of GDP. Same method for businessTransfers (2024 $286.4B), govEnterpriseSurplus (2024 -$47.5B) and depreciation (consumption of fixed capital, 2024 $4,796.7B).
incomeNotes.statisticalDiscrepancy: GDP - GDI (residual of the estimates above; BEA 2024 actual was $296.3B, 1.0% of GDP).
incomeNotes.netOperatingSurplus: Owners' share of domestic income: netInterest + businessTransfers + proprietors + rental + corporateProfitsDomestic (private enterprises).
incomeNotes.dividendsNonfinancial: Net dividends of nonfinancial corporations (Z.1, chartbook mirror), 2025 average 4.56% of GDP.

personalNotes.basis: BEA NIPA Table 2.6 (monthly personal income and outlays), 2025 = average of monthly SAAR, via the US-chartbook GitHub mirror (pi_raw.csv / nipa20600.csv), pre-Sept-2026 vintage.
personalNotes.identity: personalIncome = compensation + proprietors + rental + interest + dividends + transfers - socialInsuranceContributions; disposableIncome = personalIncome - personalTaxes; outlays = pce + interestPaid + transferPaymentsPaid; saving = disposableIncome - outlays; savingRate = saving / disposableIncome (a fraction, 0.0458 = 4.6%).
personalNotes.transfers: Personal current transfer receipts = governmentSocialBenefits (socialSecurity + medicare + medicaid + otherTransfers) + transfersFromBusiness. otherTransfers = unemployment insurance, veterans, refundable tax credits, SNAP, SSI and other benefits. Medicare and Medicaid are in-kind (paid to providers) and also appear in PCE health care.
personalNotes.interestPaid: Personal interest payments are NON-mortgage (credit cards, auto, student loans); mortgage interest is netted out of rental income/housing in NIPA. mortgageInterestPaid ($504.7B) is a CE-based estimate for owner-occupied and vacation homes (2024), for labels only.

governmentNotes.federalFiscal: receipts, individualIncomeTax, payrollTax, corporateTax, tariffs, otherReceipts, outlays, socialSecurity, medicare (net of offsetting receipts), medicaid (federal share), health (= medicare + medicaid), defense (DoD military; national defense function 050 ~$917B), netInterest (= interest), otherOutlays and deficit are FEDERAL, fiscal year 2025 (Oct 2024 - Sep 2025): CBO Monthly Budget Review Nov 2025 and Treasury MTS Sept 2025.
governmentNotes.transfers: Government social benefits to persons, all levels of government, NIPA calendar 2025 ($4,845.1B; FRED A063RC = $4,848.2B in another vintage).
governmentNotes.purchases: Government consumption expenditures and gross investment (all levels; federal; state & local), calendar 2025 ESTIMATED as BEA 2024 values (purchases2024 etc.) x nominal GDP growth 2024-25 (1.050); 2025 levels were not in the research data.
governmentNotes.stateLocalReceipts: State & local current receipts (NIPA Table 3.3), 2025 average of quarterly SAAR (Q1 3,940.3, Q2 3,923.6, Q4 4,025.0; Q3 interpolated); includes federal grants-in-aid ($992.7B SAAR in Q4).
governmentNotes.nipaQ4: Fields ending in Q4 are NIPA 2025-Q4 seasonally adjusted annual rates (BEA SCB April 2026); consolidated totals net out federal grants to state & local.

groups.name: Bottom 50%
groups.note: Mostly young households and renters (in the age model about three in four households under 40 fall here). Owns 1% of stocks and business equity, holds 30% of household debt (52% of consumer credit).
The middle class: homeowners (46% of household real estate), pension holders (47% of pension entitlements), half of all wages.
Professionals and small-business owners: 37% of stocks, 32% of private businesses, 36% of deposits and bonds.

groups.name: Top 1%
groups.note: 1.35 million households (top 0.1%: 136,000 with ~$184M each). Half of all stocks and of private business equity; ~7% of wages.

groupNotes.source: Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts (DFA), 2026:Q1 detailed levels (June 2026 release, bdecon/US-chartbook GitHub mirror of dfa-networth-levels-detail.csv). top1 = top 0.1% + 99-99.9%. households in millions, netWorth in $T (2026:Q2 headline shares: top1 32.5%, next9 36.4%, next40 28.8%, bottom50 2.3% of $185.8T).
groupNotes.businessShare: DFA share of private (non-corporate) business equity; use it for proprietors' income.
groupNotes.equityShare: DFA share of corporate equities and mutual fund shares held directly by households (incl. IRAs). Equity held through DB/DC pensions is attributed with pensionShare (DFA share of DB + DC pension entitlements), see pensionEquityShare.
groupNotes.realEstateShare: DFA share of household real estate (market value). realEstateEquityShare (value less home mortgages) is the better key for net rental income.
groupNotes.interestShare: DFA share of deposits + debt securities (task definition). Money-market funds would raise the top 1% slightly (0.30 instead of 0.28); NIPA personal interest also includes imputed interest on pensions and insurance, which is spread more like pensionShare.
groupNotes.debtShare: DFA share of home mortgages + consumer credit (bottom50 holds 52% of consumer credit and 23% of mortgages). consumerCreditShare = DFA share of consumer credit alone; use it for personal interest payments (personal.interestPaid), which are non-mortgage.
groupNotes.incomeWealthModel: Flows measured by INCOME group (wages, personal taxes, means-tested benefits) are moved to WEALTH groups with a Gumbel copula between household income rank and wealth rank (theta = 1.87, Kendall tau 0.47), fitted so the model reproduces the DFA 2026:Q1 net-worth shares of the six DFA income groups (model [2.5, 5.0, 8.4, 15.5, 44.8, 23.8] vs DFA [2.89, 4.17, 7.82, 13.33, 47.31, 24.47], %). Independent check: the implied median income rank of SCF 2022 wealth groups p0-25, 25-50, 50-75, 75-90, 90-100 is [0.23, 0.4, 0.57, 0.75, 0.92], close to the SCF 2022 medians ($35K, $59K, $83K, $141K, $302K, i.e. ranks of about 0.25, 0.43, 0.57, 0.76, 0.93). Wealth within the bottom 90% follows the SCF decile shape (chartbook wealth_dist.csv) scaled to DFA totals.
groupNotes.wageShare: Wages & salaries by DFA income group from BLS CE 2024 (wages per consumer unit by income quintile: $5.2K, $23.5K, $55.3K, $100.2K, $219.3K), with the top 1% of households by income assigned 10% of all wages (recalled: Piketty-Saez-Zucman wage-income top 1% share ~10-12%; CE barely covers the top 1%); then moved to wealth groups with the copula. Cross-check: SCF 2022 mean income by wealth group (p0-25 $44K, p25-50 $70K, p50-75 $97K, p75-90 $169K, p90-100 $633K) less realized capital gains (2021 ~$2.0T, recalled IRS SOI, assumed 85% to the top 10%), scaled to 2025 NIPA household income, minus DFA-allocated capital income and transfers, leaves ~22% / 45% / 32% (top 10%) of wages, close to the copula result (24% / 47% / 29%).
groupNotes.transferShare: Government social benefits 2025 ($4,845B) program by program: Social Security + Medicare ($2,794B) by the age profile of wealth (each DFA age group's wealth rank ~ N(mu_a, 1), mu fitted to DFA 2026:Q1 net worth by age: [-0.75, -0.04, 0.4, 0.38]), with recipients per household 0.05 / 0.10 / 0.45 / 1.0 for ages <40 / 40-54 / 55-69 / 70+; Medicaid + other means-tested ($1,722B) to income groups 50% / 27% / 13% / 7% / 3% / 0% (bottom 20% .. top 1%; approximate, after CBO household income distributions) then through the copula; unemployment insurance + veterans ($329B) per household.
groupNotes.taxShare: Personal current taxes by income group: top 1% by income pay 37.3% (= 0.8 x 40.4% of federal income tax, IRS SOI TY2022 via Tax Foundation, + 0.2 x ~25% of state & local income taxes, approximate); the rest split like BLS CE 2024 taxes by quintile (before-tax minus after-tax income; negative bottom quintile set to 0 because NIPA counts refundable credits as transfers); then through the copula.
groupNotes.consumptionShare: PCE by group = group disposable income (2025 NIPA components x the shares above) - interest paid (non-mortgage, split by consumerCreditShare) - transfers paid (per household) - saving. Saving rates by wealth: top1 35%, next9 12% (recalled: Saez & Zucman 2016 QJE synthetic saving rates by wealth class, 2000s-2010s); bottom 90% rate -4.7% solved so that group saving adds up to 2025 personal saving ($1,046.8B), the same for bottom50 and next40 (Saez-Zucman find about -5% for the bottom 90%). consumptionShareCE is the alternative from BLS CE 2024 spending by income moved through the copula; it implies a -50% saving rate for the bottom 50%, inconsistent with their balance sheet, because CE under-reports income at the bottom and spending at the top.
groupNotes.budget: personalIncome, disposableIncome, pce and saving per group ($B 2025) are the result of applying the shares to NIPA 2025 (they add up to the personal block); savingRate is saving / disposableIncome.

equityHoldersNote: foreignEquityShare = rest-of-world holdings / all US corporate equities, Fed Z.1 L.224 2025:Q4 ($20,454.9B / $111,355.4B; market commentary ~18%). pensionEquityShare = share of households' (domestic) equity exposure held through DB and DC pensions: DFA 2026:Q1 pension entitlements ($31.5T) x 0.45 equity fraction vs directly held equities & mutual funds ($55.1T) x 0.85 (equity fractions recalled: ICI/Z.1 pension-fund and mutual-fund asset mixes, approximate). Circuit use: payouts x foreignEquityShare go Abroad; the rest x pensionEquityShare is split by groups' pensionShare and the remainder by equityShare.
groupHistoryNote: Shares of household net worth. 1989-2026: Fed DFA, mean of the quarters of each year (1989: Q3-Q4; 2026: Q1 detailed + Q2 headline), computed from the levels in dfa-networth-levels-detail.csv (US-chartbook mirror). 1950-1988: Saez & Zucman (2016) top 1% and top 10% wealth shares (approximate values recalled in the research, +/-2-3 pp; anchors 1950, 1960, 1970, 1978, 1986, linear in between), spliced to DFA 1989 by scaling top1 by 0.857 and next9 by 0.984 (S-Z measures wealth per tax unit and is more concentrated than DFA); the bottom 90% is split with the DFA 1989 ratio (bottom50 = 8.8% of the bottom 90%). groupEquityHistory: DFA shares of corporate equities & mutual fund shares, 1989-2026 (2026 = Q1).

io.note: BEA 2024 summary Use table, before redefinitions, producers' prices (release 2025-09-25; GitHub mirror EthanSterling04/market-concentration-tail-risk IO_Tables/2024.csv), aggregated from the 71 BEA summary industries straight to the 25 industry ids (so software/internet, legal/professional and federal/state_local are exact splits, not value-added proxies; the design's "26 ids" are these 25 BEA-based ids, the AI overlay is not a sector). Rows are commodities (supplier), columns industries (user). Flows below $5B are dropped except diagonal (own-industry) flows: 346 flows keep $20761B of $21166B intermediate use (98.1%). Scrap/used goods and noncomparable imports ($273B of intermediate inputs) are not assigned to an industry. Mapping (same as industries.json, after DESIGN.md): oil_gas = 211+213+324, mining_metals = 212+331, hardware = 334, software = 5112+5415, internet = 514, media_telecom = 5111+512+513, legal = 5411, professional = 5412OP+55+561, other_services = 81+562 (as in industries.json); summary industry 511 (publishing incl. software) is split 85.9% software publishers / 14.1% newspaper & book publishers by their 2024 value added (BEA detail) in both its row and its column. federal = GFGD+GFGN+GFE, state_local = GSLG+GSLE. accounts = each industry's 2024 output, intermediate inputs, value added and its split (compensation, taxes on production less subsidies, gross operating surplus incl. depreciation).

finalDemandNote: 2024 $B by COMMODITY (what each industry's products are bought for), BEA 2024 summary Use table, producers' prices. pce = personal consumption expenditures; investment = private fixed investment (structures, equipment, intellectual property, residential) + change in inventories; government = federal + state & local consumption expenditures and gross investment (government's own services appear under federal / state_local); exports; imports are NEGATIVE (BEA convention: they offset final uses; wholesale trade shows a positive entry for customs duties). Trade, transport and retail margins are part of trade/transport (producers' prices), so pce for manufacturing excludes the store margin. Sum over industries + finalDemandUnallocated = BEA totals (pce 19896.0, investment 5259.3, government 5041.1, exports 2783.1, imports -3681.5); pce + investment + government + exports + imports = 2024 GDP $29,298.0B.
